Families concentrated their spending around back-to-school, and then, as our advertising intensity lessened and fuel prices increased, consumer demand softened until cold weather arrived. Early results from our merchandising work are encouraging. Customers responded to our boot assortment as soon as the season opened, and those sales carried higher average unit retails and improved margins. Fran Horowitz, Chief Executive Officer, said, “We delivered record third quarter net sales and our 16th consecutive quarter of growth, with strong customer response to our product and marketing driving results above our expectations. Growth was balanced across regions and brands, with each seeing growth rates accelerate from second quarter levels. Hollister grew 11% in the important back-to-school quarter, and Abercrombie brands grew 12%. Disciplined inventory management supported higher average unit retail with lower than expected promotions. Strong gross margin performance, coupled with operating expense leverage, led both operating margin and earnings per diluted share above our outlook. Our strong profitability and balance sheet allowed us to further invest in new stores, marketing and technology while consistently returning capital to shareholders through share repurchases, with year-to-date repurchases totaling 9% of shares outstanding as of the beginning of the year. We’re energized by the momentum across our business as we enter the holiday season, and we are increasing our expectations for full-year net sales and earnings per share. We remain on track for another year of record net sales, strong double-digit operating margins and growth in earnings per share. Combined with consistent, significant share repurchases, we expect our performance in fiscal 2026 will further demonstrate the durability of our operating model and add to our track record of creating sustainable, profitable growth.” A summary of results for the third quarter ended October 31, 2026 as compared to the third quarter ended November 1, 2025: •Net sales of $1.4 billion, up 11% as compared to last year, with comparable sales up 6%. •Operating income of $223 million, including approximately $20 million in refunds of IEEPA tariffs reflected as a reduction of cost of sales as compared to operating income of $155 million last year. •Operating margin as a percent of sales of 15.5% as compared to 12.0% last year. •Net income per diluted share of $3.82 as compared to net income per diluted share last year of $2.36.
